correctness.rationale: The fully absorbing disk backward Poisson problem has passive mean (1-s^2)/4. Its order-p first harmonic solves a modified-Bessel radial Dirichlet equation; the averaged order-p^2 term obeys w′=-h/2. Integration yields the explicit C_g(s). Substituting u=-h=s f in the first-harmonic equation gives exactly (-Delta_4+g)f=1/2 in the four-ball. The killed Brownian resolvent is a Laplace integral with a strictly positive integrand, proving (-1)^n partial_g^n C_g(s)>0 for all nonnegative integers and interior s. Direct polynomial and Bessel asymptotic calculations give both endpoints. The 25 independently shot radial ODE comparisons, 60 derivative spot-checks and exact symbolic polynomial identities in verify.py all passed; finite checks only corroborate the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Weak-activity sensitivity of a fully absorbing active Brownian disk is a natural quantitative first-exit observable explicitly proposed as further work in the source paper. The explicit coefficient at every radius gives a sharp enhancement rate and a non-obvious universal complete-monotonicity law under changing angular diffusion, together with exact persistent and rapidly mixing endpoint behavior. The four-dimensional resolvent lift explains the structural sign law, rather than merely recalculating a known stationary density or a finite sample. The result does not claim an independent theorem about arbitrary propulsion strengths.
